Selection precedence changed. Candidate places DatabricksOauthProfileMapping before DatabricksTokenProfileMapping (generated/cosmos/profiles/__init__.py:35-36). The reference places it after (reference/cosmos/profiles/__init__.py:35-36). Original has only the token mapping (base/cosmos/profiles/__init__.py:34).

Selection is first-claim (base/cosmos/profiles/__init__.py:61-64). DatabricksTokenProfileMapping claims any connection where the password is set, because token maps from ['password','extra.token'] (base/cosmos/profiles/databricks/token.py:35; base/cosmos/profiles/base.py:284-302) and can_claim only checks truthiness (base/cosmos/profiles/base.py:154-183). A connection with login + password + http_path + schema is therefore claimed by token in the original and in the reference, but by OAuth in the candidate.
The candidate's own test encodes this shift: generated/tests/profiles/databricks/test_dbr_oauth.py:76-86 asserts OAuth is selected for a connection with login and password.
Only the no-login case keeps token selection (generated/tests/profiles/databricks/test_dbr_oauth.py:89-102). That case is unchanged.

Trade-off to weigh: the reference's ordering means standard login+password OAuth connections are also claimed by token, so the reference's OAuth mapping auto-selects only when no password is present. The candidate's ordering is arguably more useful for OAuth, but it silently re-routes existing login+password token connections, which the reference and original do not do.

Client-id handling diverges. Reference treats client_id as a secret: secret_fields includes it (reference/cosmos/profiles/databricks/oauth.py:29), it is env-var-ed (:46-47), and the docstring states it (:41). Candidate keeps it as a literal (generated/cosmos/profiles/databricks/oauth.py:32-34, 39, 48), and its test locks that in (generated/tests/profiles/databricks/test_dbr_oauth.py:131).
criteria.deficiency: Two behavioral deviations from the reference. (1) Ordering: placing the OAuth mapping ahead of the token mapping changes which mapping existing login+password Databricks connections receive, which is a backward-compatibility change the reference does not make. (2) client_id: the candidate does not treat the OAuth client ID as a secret or env var, contrary to the reference's stated behavior. The candidate's own tests lock in both deviations, so they would not catch them.
